adr: ADR 0039 — The encoding a font program brings with it
source_slice: §9.8.2 prose on physical 360–361, especially the paragraph saying a processor should always check Symbolic when Symbolic/Nonsymbolic conflict; Table 121 bits 3 and 6.
current_decision: Use the Symbolic bit as the discriminator, including when an invalid writer-produced word sets both bits; do not let Nonsymbolic override it.
review: The selected unit test independently makes the symbolic and nonsymbolic cmap routes return different glyph IDs and verifies each single-bit control plus both-set behavior. This is correctly framed as the source's processor recommendation, not a new SHALL to reject contradictory producer data.

adr: ADR 1074 — A glyph class is decided by the character
source_slice: §9.8.3.3 and Table 123, physical 364–365; Table 123 defines several classes by what glyphs represent, while some classes distinguish form/usage rather than a character identity.
current_decision: Apply a class override only when the Unicode character evidence can distinguish the listed class; preserve the main descriptor and report classes the reader cannot determine from that evidence.
review: The current classifier's single/overlap/example cases and collection-specific positive/negative controls support the premise. The public class-face test separately checks the consequence. This does not claim that the standard prescribes the exact substitute face, or that Unicode alone resolves rotated, ruby, dingbat, or generic glyphs.
status: selected rationale remains supported; all-table-cell public rendering not claimed

adr: ADR 2817 — A Type 1 font in an OpenType wrapper is read by its glyph names
source_slice: §9.9.1 Table 124, physical 367–368; the Type1 dictionary + CFF table route is distinct from TrueType + glyf and CID CFF routes.
current_decision: Choose glyph lookup by the font dictionary and contained program/table combination; a Type1 dictionary over name-keyed OpenType CFF uses the Type1 name-keyed route.
review: The current exact-xref test includes same-program OpenType-CFF and bare-Type1C cases, and distinct real OpenType glyf and CFF cases under simple and CID dictionaries. Literal glyph-index expectations differ across branches, so it is not a shared-route/round-trip oracle. The fixture fonts are usable real programs but the test is not an independent ISO/IEC 14496-22 validator.
status: selected decision has direct route assertions; standards conformance residual remains

adr: ADR 0049 — A CID into a Type 1 program
source_slice: Table 124's listed CIDFont program combinations versus the ADR's observed `/FontFile` on CIDFontType0.
current_decision: The implementation supports an additional reader path for the encountered bare Type1/CIDFont case by analogy with name-keyed CFF.
review: This ADR is not evidence that Table 124 lists FontFile as a permitted CIDFont embedding. Its adopted compatibility decision should remain separate from the table's producer mapping; no test in this shard treats the non-listed combination as a required valid case.
